theme-monad-gcc-real-states ran the shipped gcc 15.2.0 emitter on real states only at 12 literal-count SHL and SHR sites of the 128 un-entered value blocks (2,138 states logged). The non-literal MUL, DIV, MOD, the all-ones MULMOD, ADD, SUB, comparisons, memory, storage and terminator emit functions were not run on those states, and the runtime 256-bit multiply, divide and mulmod helpers were not run from the package. The unit rated the follow-up low, but these are the FullMath.mulDiv 512-bit blocks (0x5757, 0x57ca, 0x5860, 0x588a, 0x58d6, 0x58db) that any account can enter in one transaction and that every validator runs from the same gcc build, so the priority is understated.

leads.question: From research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-monad-gcc-real-states.work/out/states.jsonl, run the shipped gcc 15.2.0 emit functions for the non-literal MUL, DIV, MOD and the all-ones-modulus MULMOD in FullMath blocks 0x5757, 0x57ca, 0x5860, 0x588a, 0x58d6 and 0x58db on their logged states. Do the argument registers and saved live set at each call to the 256-bit multiply, divide and mulmod runtime helpers match the clang listing up to renaming? Then run those helpers from the package text on 10,000 operand sets with the mulDiv shapes of tools/opdiff/v4math.py. Does any word differ from pyevm.py?
leads.why: These blocks compute FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24-91), which every swap step and fee growth value reads. Every Monad validator runs the same gcc build, no mined transaction since v0.16.7 has entered them, and any account can enter them, so a wrong word there would be certified and would mis-price a swap against ordinary LPs.

leads.question: Between base v1.5.6 and v1.6.0-rc.9, did the B20 token precompile crate change how it writes balances (EvmInternals.sstore into the revm journal) or how its frame checkpoint is committed or reverted? Fetch both trees' B20 precompile sources from raw.githubusercontent.com and compare. Then place TokenRollbackProbe (cycle 16) at the PoolManager address and run it on mainnet.base.org for OUSD in a reverted, a halted and a static inner frame.
leads.why: op-stack-eth checked only the interpreter and the integer library pins of rc.9. If a B20 write escaped the journal, a take inside a frame that then reverts would keep the tokens while the delta rolls back (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:53-86). The Base PoolManager holds about 5.34 million OUSD in pools with no attacker hook or token.

leads.question: On 8 December 2026 after 02:30 UTC, place TokenRollbackProbe at the PoolManager address on bsc-dataseed1 and on bsc-rpc.publicnode.com (reth-bsc). For one live CAS20 token, does a transfer from the PoolManager inside a reverted, a halted and a static inner frame leave both balances unchanged, and does a returning frame move exactly the amount? Are the success flag and return data of a CAS20 transfer that runs out of gas in finishCAS20Metered the same on geth and reth-bsc?
leads.why: Cycle 16 could not run this on BNB Chain because CAS20 was not active. CAS20 is a stateful token precompile implemented twice, in bsc geth and in reth-bsc, whose own crates are unread. A write that escaped the journal would let a take keep tokens after the frame and the delta revert.

leads.question: In the bor v2.11.2 amd64 binary, is the 64-byte keccak cache read by opKeccak256 (instructions.go:265-278) a process-wide object shared by BlockSTM workers? Are its Get and Add guarded by a lock, and is the stored value a copied array or a slice into the interpreter's reused hasherBuf? Read the cache's methods from pclntab and the disassembly.
leads.why: Every CurrencyDelta slot (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:14) and every mapping slot is a 64-byte keccak. A torn or aliased cache entry under parallel execution would point a delta or pool write at the wrong slot. The theme read the key compare in source only, not the concurrency of the shipped object.

leads.question: In the bsc v1.8.2, bor v2.11.2 and avalanchego v1.15.3 binaries already in the go-family work directory, do opTstore, opTload, the transientStorageChange and storageChange revert methods and RevertToSnapshot restore the previous value in the x86-64 model? Use the Nitro theme's sequences (20,007 sequences over the PoolManager's slot shapes, with nested reverts and equal-value writes).
leads.why: The settlement ledger is transient (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol, src/libraries/Lock.sol). A delta that survives a reverted frame would let a caller keep a credit it never paid. These three chains are the only go-family networks whose storage path has not been run from the binary.
